parent_definitions.definition: An entity that perceives some part of its environment and acts on it in pursuit of goals — its own, or those of another party on whose behalf it acts. The genus is neutral about substrate: people, organizations, software and collectives can all be agents. What sets an agent apart from other entities is directed action, not what it is made of.

An entity intentionally produced by an agent to serve a purpose, whose identity depends on its author's productive intention and intended function rather than on natural-kind membership. Artifacts are evaluated against the purposes they were designed to fulfill.

An event that is a bounded communicative exchange among participants over a communication channel — e.g., a meeting, thread, pairing session, DM exchange, or review. The perdurant unit at which collaboration episodes are scored.
A Cognitive_Entity is an Entity capable of performing cognitive processes, such as perception, memory, reasoning, learning, or decision-making.
An Entity is a Thing whose existence the describing ontology assumes, whether concrete or abstract and individual or collective, and that can bear properties and stand in relations to other entities.

Something that happens at a specific time, with a beginning and an end; a bounded occurrent that may involve persons, be hosted by an organization, and produce documents or result in decisions. (L459 core entity, here promoted from vision YAML to instantiated concept.)

An entity that unfolds through time, having temporal parts and a beginning and end — as opposed to a continuant, which is wholly present at every moment of its existence. The top category under which events, processes, sessions, and activities fall.

A system for which software is of primary importance to the stakeholders — a combination of interacting elements (software, hardware, data, human procedures) organized to achieve one or more stated purposes, where software is the principal locus of functionality. The unit of process governance under ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017.

A combination of interacting elements organized to achieve one or more stated purposes, where the whole exhibits properties not reducible to its components considered in isolation. A system is bounded, structured, and goal-directed.
A Thing is anything that can be referred to, named, or made the subject of discourse, whether concrete or abstract.
